amendments.normalized_body: In `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs`, the committed constant `FILTER_MEDIA_CM2_PER_LITER = 200.0` scales filter media area proportionally to tank volume in `scale_hardware_to_geometry()`. For a 2× size_scale tank (8× volume ≈ 160L), media_area jumps from 2000 to 32000 cm², diluting nitrifier density and causing biofilter maturation to stall (maturity 0.017 vs expected 0.06+). The working tree already has an uncommitted fix removing this scaling — commit and apply that fix. Filter media area should remain a hardware specification (default 2000 cm²), not auto-scale with volume.

In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs` line 227, `plant_shading` is applied uniformly to all periphyton habitats including GlassHardscape. Glass wall periphyton receives direct lateral light and should be less affected by plant canopy shading than substrate-surface periphyton. Consider making plant_shading habitat-weighted (e.g., full effect on SubstrateSurface, reduced on GlassHardscape/PlantSurfaces) to avoid artificially suppressing glass biofilm growth in planted tanks.

In `crates/tank_core/tests/end_to_end.rs` lines 276-289 (uncommitted working change), the `happy_plants_grow_with_light_and_nutrients` assertion was relaxed from `>= initial_biomass` to `>= initial_biomass * 0.80`. If geometry-scaled initial biomass causes plants to self-shade and decline by 20% under 'happy' conditions (good light, good nutrients), this suggests the PLANT_BIOMASS_G_PER_1000_CM2_FOOTPRINT constant (6.0 g/1000cm²) may overshoot for smaller tanks or the self-shading model is too aggressive. Validate the constant against actual scenario footprints before committing the relaxed assertion.

`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:503-516` and `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:744-752` stop scaling `filter.media_area_cm2`, but seeded scenarios still have no way to supply a replacement hardware-specific value (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:220-234`, `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1864-1877`). Because `FilterHardware::default()` hard-codes 2000 cm2 (`crates/tank_core/src/types/hardware.rs:77-90`), every seeded tank now materializes with the same filter-media habitat area regardless of size while flow still scales with volume. That collapses size-dependent biofilter/habitat differences and makes startup scenarios ecologically incorrect. Restore geometry scaling or add an explicit scenario/startup media-area parameter before removing the old rule.

`crates/tank_core/tests/end_to_end.rs:257-289` weakens `happy_plants_grow_with_light_and_nutrients` from a growth assertion to an `>= 80%` survivability check without fixing the underlying regression. The test name and doc comment still say plants grow under good light and nutrients, but the suite now passes even when that happy-path scenario loses 20% of its biomass. This removes an important end-to-end guard for a user-visible regression instead of addressing the cause.
